cards.title: Introduction to Vue Templates
cards.content:
Vue.js uses an HTML-based template syntax that allows you to declaratively bind the rendered DOM to the underlying component instance's data.

All Vue templates are syntactically valid HTML that can be parsed by spec-compliant browsers and HTML parsers.

cards.title: Text Interpolation
cards.content:
The most basic form of data binding is text interpolation using the "Mustache" syntax (double curly braces).

<span>Message: {{ msg }}</span>

The mustache tag will be replaced with the value of the msg property from the corresponding component instance.

cards.title: Attribute Bindings with v-bind
cards.content:
Mustaches cannot be used inside HTML attributes. Instead, use a v-bind directive:

<div v-bind:id="dynamicId"></div>

Because v-bind is so commonly used, there is a dedicated shorthand syntax:

<div :id="dynamicId"></div>

cards.title: Complete the Directive Shorthand
cards.content: To dynamically bind an attribute to a data property in Vue without typing 'v-bind:', you can use the shorthand symbol ______ before the attribute name.

cards.title: Directives Overview
cards.content:
Directives are special attributes with the v- prefix. Vue provides many built-in directives, such as v-if, v-for, and v-on.

They expect a single JavaScript expression as their value (with the exception of v-for, v-on, and v-bind).

cards.title: Event Handling with v-on
cards.content:
You can use the v-on directive (shorthand @) to listen to DOM events and run JavaScript when they're triggered.

<button @click="count++">Add 1</button>
<p>Count is: {{ count }}</p>

cards.title: Summary of Vue Templates
cards.content:
Vue templates bridge the gap between plain HTML and dynamic JavaScript data. Key takeaways:

  • Use {{ }} for text interpolation.
  • Use v-bind (or :) for attributes.
  • Use v-on (or @) for events.
  • Leverage directives like v-if and v-for for control flow.
